title: Influence of the averaged neighbor function
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with alphabet size $q$, let $T$ assign to each vertex a function on the $q$-dimensional Boolean cube taking values in $[-1,1]$, and fix a vertex $v$ and coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}$. The influence of coordinate $i$ in the function obtained by averaging the twisted neighbor functions at $v$ is at most the average, over neighbors $w$ of $v$, of the influence of coordinate $\pi_{v,w}^{-1}(i)$ in $T(w)$, where $\pi_{v,w}$ is the edge permutation.
hypotheses_covered: A regular unique game $G$ with alphabet size $q$
A bounded cube function assigned to each vertex
